system_overview: This specification models a system that alternately performs two actions, referred to as the zeroth and first actions. A control variable alternates between zero and one, triggering the corresponding action on each transition. This captures the fundamental pattern of two processes taking turns, abstracted away from any particular implementation.
actors_and_components: The system is parameterized by two constant operators: one describing valid initial states for the data component, and one describing valid transitions for each of the two alternating actions. The actors are implicit: the zeroth action corresponds to one party (e.g., a producer) and the first action to the other party (e.g., a consumer).
state_variables: The system tracks two pieces of state: (1) A control variable that alternates between zero and one, indicating which action should occur next. (2) A data variable representing the application-specific state that is modified by each action.
initial_state: The control variable starts at zero. The data variable satisfies the initial-state predicate provided as a constant parameter.
actions: A single next-state relation: the control variable advances from its current value to the next (cycling between zero and one using modular arithmetic), and the data variable is updated according to the action predicate corresponding to the current control value. The zeroth action fires when the control is zero, and the first action fires when the control is one.
additional_assumptions: The specification uses higher-order constant operators: a unary predicate for initial data states and a ternary predicate relating the action index, current data value, and next data value. A note observes that a philosophically complete specification would hide the control variable using existential quantification, but this is omitted for practical engineering reasons.
